outcome: Pass rates of AABR, DPOAE, and AI hearing screenings
cohort: 2,194 high-risk neonates admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) of Shanghai Children's Medical Center from January 2015 to December 2019
finding: Hearing screening pass rates, particularly for AABR, were lower in high-risk neonates compared to healthy controls, with risk factors including NRDS, hyperbilirubinemia, low birth weight, advanced maternal age, congenital heart disease, C-section, and artificial feeding.
mod_finding: C-section was negatively correlated with pass rates for both DPOAE and AI hearing screenings.
birth_weight: Low birth weight (LBW) and very low birth weight (VLBW) were analyzed as risk factors for hearing screening failure.
